difficultyReason: Infer the inverted absolute-value function from its vertex and a point, then classify slopes of lines through the origin by whether they meet both restricted rays at distinct points, including the vertex and parallel boundaries. This requires connecting algebraic or geometric intersection conditions to the graph rather than simply applying a transformation.

derivation.diagram: The code draws an inverted V with vertex (6,7), left slope 4 and right slope -4, continuing downwards on both rays. The plotted points (3,-5) and (9,-5) lie on the respective rays. There are no multiple-choice options.
derivation.partA: The vertex gives b=6 and c=7. Substituting (3,-5) yields -5=3a+7, so a=-4. Thus f(x)=-4|x-6|+7.
derivation.partB: The left branch is y=4x-17 for x<=6 and the right branch is y=-4x+31 for x>=6. Their intersections with y=mx have xL=17/(4-m), xR=31/(m+4), when denominators are nonzero. The left branch is met when m<=7/6 or m>4; the right branch is met only when -4<m<=7/6. Both are met distinctly precisely for -4<m<7/6. At m=7/6 they coincide at the vertex; at m=-4 the origin line is parallel to and distinct from the right ray. For m>4 the right-branch algebraic intersection has negative x and lies outside x>=6, so the historical extra interval is invalid.
